item.title: Stable, High-Charge, Laser-Driven VHEE Beams for Preclinical Applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.09329v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Laser-driven plasma accelerators (LPAs) are promising sources of very-high-energy-electron (VHEE) beams for medical applications, but increasing charge per pulse while maintaining pointing stability remains challenging. We demonstrate laser-accelerated beams with total charge per pulse reaching (559 $\pm$ 56) pC using an 80 TW laser system. The spectra have a dominant component at 40-60 MeV and a high-energy tail extending to approximately 200 MeV. Pointing jitter measured in air at the irradiation target plane reaches as low as 0.7 mrad. The beams were used for VHEE irradiation experiments involving a 10 mm region of interest through a 40 mm depth at 400 $\pm$ 20 mGy/pulse. Spectral reproducibility is quantified over fixed-setting shot sequences. Particle-in-cell simulations produce a peak-and-tail spectrum through acceleration in successive bubbles associated with a strongly modified plasma wake, providing a plausible mechanism for maintaining substantial accelerated charge despite strong beam loading. Dose-weighted time-of-flight calculations indicate an effective pulse dose rate of $10^{12}$ Gy/s and average dose rates of tens of Gy/min. These results establish an LPA operating regime relevant to preclinical VHEE irradiation.
item.dc:creator: Chaitanya Varma, Camilla Giaccaglia, Julien Gautier, Jean-Philippe Goddet, Amar Tafzi, Pascal Rousseau, Alessandro Flacco

item.title: Secondary neutron beam production at Jefferson Lab
item.description: arXiv:2611.09525v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate secondary neutron production by an 11 GeV electron beam in the Hall A beam dump at Jefferson Lab and their transport to a downstream experimental area. This secondary beam could operate opportunistically with the primary electron-scattering programme. The neutron energy spectrum extends from thermal energies to several GeVs, offering a distinctive opportunity for irradiation at energy grater than 1 GeV. We considered three configurations: the current setup, the planned BDX facility, and an optimized BDX layout with a dedicated neutron extraction pipe. We also studied how radiators made of different materials and placed upstream of the beam dump increase neutron production.
item.dc:creator: A. Fulci, P. Ambrozewicz, M. Battaglieri, M. Bondi, R. De Vita, M. Filippini, G. Foti, S. Grazzi, G. Mandaglio, T. Nagorna, A. Pilloni, M. Spreafico, S. Vallarino

item.title: Portable Glass-RPC Telescope for Muography and Future Applications at Laser Wake Field Accelerators
item.description: arXiv:2611.09541v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We report a 2025 beam test at ELBA, the multi-GeV laser wakefield accelerator at ELI Beamlines, using a Resistive Plate Chamber (RPC) telescope with an active area of 16 * 16 cm2. The portable design sup- ports autonomous operation in challenging environments. Previous cosmic-ray measurements established its tracking capability for muography. During the campaign at ELBA, 30 f s long, 0.5 PW laser pulses in- teracted with a plasma target at a 0.2 Hz repetition rate, where a tungsten converter upstream of the beam dump enhanced muon production. This was the first deployment of an RPC telescope in a high-power laser environment. The detector remained operational in the presence of radiation and electromagnetic interference. Although parasitic running and limited statistics prevented definitive identification of beam- induced muons, the measurements offered insight into background activity and showed evidence of re- constructed tracks. They establish the feasibility of a dedicated campaign with controlled beam conditions and improved muon sensitivity. This contribution forms part of the International Muography Workshop 2026 proceedings.
item.dc:creator: S. Ikram, D. Ahmadi, U. Chaulagain, A. Cimmino, E. Cortina Gil, P. Demin, A. Giammanco, G. M. Grittani, M. Lagrange, M. Nevrkla, J. Sisma, M. Tytgat, R. Versaci, F. Vitha

item.title: Quantum trajectory perspective of atom-field interaction in attosecond time scale
item.description: arXiv:physics/0607110v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Here the ionization and high harmonic generation in Hydrogen and Helium by using quantum (hydrodynamic) trajectories is analyzed theoretically. The quantum trajectories allow a self-contained treatment of the electron exchange and correlation effects without introducing ad hoc potentials into the Schrodinger equation. Our approach predicts the correct high harmonic spectra and the attosecond pulses generated by the Helium atom beyond the single active electron approximation. It can be used to study complex multi-electron systems and their interaction with laser field of both high and low intensity.
item.dc:creator: Ivan P. Christov
